standard.title: Deliver elaborated presentations
standard.description: plan, create, rehearse and deliver short oral and/or multimodal presentations to inform and persuade
standard.prior_knowledge: Students create, rehearse and deliver short presentations for familiar audiences, varying tone, volume and pace (AC9E2LY07). They have not yet planned and researched content for presentations, or used storyboards and sequencing as planning tools.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students plan, create, rehearse and deliver short oral and/or multimodal presentations to inform and persuade.

nodes.label: Planning and researching a presentation
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can research a topic and plan the sequence of ideas for a presentation using planning techniques such as storyboards.
nodes.minimum_width: Research a topic for a presentation, gather at least three facts or ideas, and plan the sequence using a simple storyboard or list.
nodes.typical_width: Research a topic to prepare an oral or multimodal presentation; plan the sequence of ideas and information using techniques such as storyboards; explain ideas to a peer when planning.
wider: Compare how planning a multimodal presentation differs from planning an oral-only one — discussing what additional decisions are needed
Explain the planned presentation to a peer before delivery and use their feedback to make at least one improvement to the plan
nodes.hinge_reason: Students who have not planned and sequenced their presentation content cannot deliver at N2 — there is no content to pace or adjust tone for.

response_modes.reason: Planning and sequencing a presentation is a procedural skill that develops through repeated practice across different topics and presentation types. Students need multiple opportunities to plan before the process becomes reliable enough to support deliberate delivery at N2.

success_criteria: Student produces a plan (storyboard, list or outline) that shows sequenced ideas before delivery
Student's plan includes enough content for a complete presentation — not just a title

nodes.label: Delivering with adjusted tone and pace
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can deliver a short oral or multimodal presentation that adjusts tone and pace to suit the purpose and audience.
nodes.minimum_width: Deliver a short presentation making at least one deliberate adjustment to tone or pace (e.g. slowing down for an important point, using an enthusiastic tone for persuasion).
nodes.typical_width: Adjust tone and pace to purpose and audience during delivery — informative presentations use clear, measured pace; persuasive presentations use engaging tone and appropriate emphasis.
wider: Record and review a presentation delivery, identifying one moment where tone or pace could be improved and why
Compare two deliveries of the same content with different tone choices and discuss which is more effective for the stated purpose

response_modes.reason: Deliberate voice control in delivery requires rehearsal — the skill develops through practice, not through more conceptual instruction about what tone and pace are. Students need multiple delivery opportunities across different presentation types.

success_criteria: Student delivers content clearly and at an appropriate pace for the audience
Student demonstrates at least one deliberate tonal or pacing choice that suits the purpose
